paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minADE₂₀ (a metric for trajectory prediction accuracy) as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linearly scaled from 0 to 8 with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←)”, is also linearly scaled, ranging from 8.80 to 10.20 with tick marks at 0.20 intervals. For the ST-ES method, the minADE₂₀ starts at 10.20 when no examples are provided, drops sharply to 9.20 at 1 example, and then gradually decreases to approximately 8.88 at 8 examples, showing a consistent improvement with more examples. In contrast, the Random method begins at 9.80 with 0 examples, decreases slightly to around 9.40 at 2 examples, and then remains relatively stable between 9.40 and 9.60 across the remaining number of examples, indicating minimal improvement beyond 2 examples.
